scope: Public citations, PDF identities and recorded retrieval/inspection status only; no source bodies.
edition_preparation_pdf_rehash_scope: Retained PDF bytes were rehashed only to confirm that the complete source packet remained frozen. No new retrieval, visual inspection or independent scholarly proof audit was performed.

sources.title: Some problems on mapping class groups and moduli space
sources.version_status: Chapter 2 of Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics, edited by Benson Farb.
sources.recorded_inspection: Printed page 29, equation (9), Conjecture 3.16 and the separate logarithmic-density definition were visually inspected during both the proof attempt and audit. Closed oriented-surface convention on printed page 10 was checked in extracted text.
sources.reliance: Exact original ambient distinct-element word-ball definition and conjecture; all-generating-set interpretation is stated expressly in the report.

sources.title: Pseudo-Anosovs are exponentially generic in mapping class groups
sources.version_status: arXiv:2110.06678v3, 25 September 2022; Geometry & Topology 28 (2024), 1923-1955. No retained-to-published PDF byte-identity claim.
sources.recorded_inspection: Theorem A, Corollary 1.1 and Question 1.4 were visually inspected during both the proof attempt and audit. The arXiv metadata was read on 10 October 2026. The complete source proof was not re-audited.
sources.reliance: Suitable enlarged generating sets versus arbitrary generating sets; the exceptional non-pseudo-Anosov set does not include all Torelli elements.

sources.title: The lower central series and pseudo-Anosov dilatations
sources.version_status: arXiv:math/0603675v2, 26 August 2007. The retained PDF title-page date of 26 November 2024 appears to be a rendering timestamp; no new 2024 mathematical revision is inferred.
sources.recorded_inspection: Theorem 1.1 on page 2 and the Teichmuller translation discussion on page 1 were visually inspected during both the proof attempt and audit. No numerical dilatation bound is needed by the proof.
sources.reliance: Existence of a pseudo-Anosov in Torelli for every closed genus g>=2 and the standard positive Teichmuller translation fact.

text_only_source.title: Normalizers and centralizers of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes
text_only_source.version_status: Author manuscript dated 8 June 1994; states it was originally written 5 March 1982.
text_only_source.recorded_inspection: The web PDF parser exposed page 1 Theorem 1 and Corollary 2, including the orientable connected compact negative-Euler-characteristic surface hypothesis; the author abstract corroborated the centralizer theorem. The independent audit read both text sources.
text_only_source.reliance: The pseudo-Anosov centralizer is virtually infinite cyclic; closed genus g>=2 is within the stated hypotheses.
text_only_source.screenshot_limitation: The screenshot request did not expose inspectable image pixels.

bounded_literature_context: The recorded 10 October 2026 primary-source pass covered Torelli density, ambient word balls, normal-subgroup negligibility, logarithmic density and the exact conjecture. No exact arbitrary-generating-set solution was located in that bounded pass; this is not an exhaustive continuing-openness or novelty certificate. No additional literature search was performed during edition preparation.
